title: Cisco C9800 WLC AP Join Failures
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Cisco C9800 WLC AP Join Failures' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_cisco_c9800_wlc_ap_join_failures` (UC-5.4.38), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Cisco C9800 WLC AP Join Failures", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=network` sourcetype='cisco:ios' that satisfy the UC-5.4.38 SPL filters for 'Cisco C9800 WLC AP Join Failures'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `network` / `cisco:ios` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.4.38.

dataSources: Cisco Catalyst 9800 wireless LAN controller syslog ingested via `TA-cisco_ios` (Splunkbase 1352). Look for the CAPWAP and DTLS facilities at severity 3 and below: `%CAPWAP-3-ERRORLOG`, `%DTLS-3-HANDSHAKE_FAILURE`, `%AP_EVENT-3-CRASH`. The AP name is normally extractable from the message body via the `AP <name>` literal.
app: Cisco Networks Add-on for Splunk (`TA-cisco_ios`, Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=network sourcetype="cisco:ios" host="c9800*"
  ("%CAPWAP-3-ERRORLOG" OR "%DTLS-3-HANDSHAKE_FAILURE" OR "%AP_EVENT-3-CRASH")
| rex "AP (?<ap_name>\S+)"
| stats count by host, ap_name, _raw
| sort - count
description: Surfaces APs that fail to register with the Cisco Catalyst 9800 wireless LAN controller because of CAPWAP tunnel failures, DTLS certificate-handshake errors, or repeated AP-side crashes. Each failed-join event represents one AP's worth of campus Wi-Fi coverage going dark.
value: Cisco Catalyst 9800 wireless controllers are the campus Wi-Fi backbone for thousands of enterprises. AP join failures are uniquely silent: the AP looks 'present' on the wired switch port (LLDP, MAC table, PoE) but never finishes handshaking with the WLC, so users in that coverage cell get no Wi-Fi at all. Three classic failure modes converge here — expired or untrusted controller certificates, CAPWAP MTU / firewall mismatches between AP and WLC, and AP-side crashes that should have triggered a hardware-replacement workflow but did not. Detection at the controller is the only place all three are visible together.
implementation: Forward Cisco C9800 syslog to Splunk at severity 3 or lower so the CAPWAP / DTLS / AP_EVENT facilities reach the indexer. Alert when any AP triggers a join failure or repeatedly crashes inside a 15-minute window. Correlate with the certificate-expiry calendar for the WLC trustpoint — most surprise outages trace back to expired CAs.
visualization: Table (failed APs with cause), Status grid (AP join state per WLC, coloured by health), Timeline (join failures over time, useful for spotting controller-wide flap events).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'Cisco C9800 WLC AP Join Failures'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `network` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Cisco Networks Add-on for Splunk (`TA-cisco_ios`, Splunkbase 1352)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ios into network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_raw, ap_name, host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the wireless access points on the ceiling check in with the building's main Wi-Fi controller. When any of them fail to check in, that part of the office loses Wi-Fi entirely — even though the device looks alive on the wall. We alert before users start asking why their phones say no signal.
